summary: LLM observability tools give teams visibility into how their AI applications behave in production by tracing requests, evaluating output quality, monitoring latency and errors, and tracking token-based API costs. As LLM usage scales, these tools are essential for controlling spend, debugging non-deterministic behavior, and maintaining reliability and quality. Without observability, teams fly blind on cost overruns, prompt regressions, and degraded user experience.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces, token usage, latency, cost, prompt/chain performance, and evaluation metrics for LLM and agent applications (especially LangChain-based).
features: Deep tracing of chains, agents, and tool calls
Dataset-driven evaluations and LLM-as-judge scoring
Prompt management and versioning (Prompt Hub)
Online and offline evals with human feedback collection
Tight native integration with LangChain and LangGraph
Production monitoring dashboards and alerting
tools.pricing: Free Developer tier with limited traces; Plus plan ~$39/user/month. Base traces (14-day retention) cost ~$2.50 per 1k and extended traces (400-day retention) ~$5.00 per 1k beyond the included allowance. Reported at roughly $264 per 100,000 traces on Plus.
tools.best_for: Teams building on LangChain/LangGraph who want first-class tracing, evaluation, and prompt iteration in one integrated platform.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API request/response logs, token usage, cost per model/user/session, latency, caching efficiency, and rate-limit behavior via a proxy or async logging.
features: One-line proxy integration for request logging
Per-user and per-session cost tracking and segmentation
Prompt caching to reduce duplicate API calls
Rate limiting and retry controls
Custom properties for filtering and analytics
Longer data retention than many competitors
tools.pricing: Free tier available; Pro at $79/month, Team at $799/month, plus enterprise. Roughly $79 per 100,000 traces with 30-day data retention.
tools.best_for: Cost-conscious teams wanting fast, lightweight integration and strong cost/usage analytics with caching to cut API spend.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompts, model experiments, evaluations, and production metrics via W&B Weave, alongside traditional ML experiment tracking.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
Experiment tracking and model/artifact versioning
Interactive dashboards and reports for collaboration
Scorers and evaluation pipelines for LLM output quality
Framework-agnostic SDK integrations
Enterprise-grade governance and team collaboration
tools.pricing: Free personal tier; paid plans (Pro/Teams) typically usage- and seat-based starting around $50/user/month, with custom enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: ML and AI teams already using W&B for experiment tracking who want unified observability across classic ML and LLM workflows.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production LLM and ML performance, traces, embeddings/drift, response quality, hallucination and relevance evals, latency, and cost.
features: Open-source Arize Phoenix for tracing and evaluation
LLM-as-judge evals for hallucination, relevance, toxicity
Embedding and data drift detection
Troubleshooting dashboards with root-cause analysis
OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation
Quality-aware alerting and monitoring at scale
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open source (self-hostable); Arize AX offers a free tier with paid Pro and custom enterprise plans based on volume.
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing robust production ML/LLM monitoring, drift detection, and research-grade evaluation at scale.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: Traces, spans, token usage, cost, latency, prompt versions, and evaluation scores for LLM and agent applications.
features: Open-source and self-hostable observability platform
Detailed nested tracing of chains and agents
Prompt management and versioning
Evaluations with LLM-as-judge and human annotation
Cost and token tracking per model and trace
Framework-agnostic SDKs and OpenTelemetry support
tools.pricing: Free open-source self-hosted option; managed cloud has a free Hobby tier, Core/Pro plans starting around $59/month, plus enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, self-hostable observability stack with strong tracing, prompt management, and data control.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, traces, token usage, latency, and costs through OpenTelemetry-based standardized telemetry exported to any compatible backend.
features: Open-source OpenTelemetry extensions for LLMs
Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs and vector DBs
Vendor-neutral export to any OTel-compatible backend
Non-intrusive, standards-based instrumentation
Integrates with existing APM/observability stacks
Powers Traceloop's managed observability offering
tools.pricing: Free and open source. Costs depend on the chosen OpenTelemetry backend; Traceloop's managed service offers a free tier with paid plans.
tools.best_for: Engineering teams that want open, standards-based (OpenTelemetry) instrumentation integrated into their existing observability infrastructure.

cost_tips: Cache repeated or similar requests (e.g., with prompt/response caching) so identical queries don't trigger new paid API calls.
Route requests to the cheapest model that meets quality needs, reserving larger frontier models only for complex tasks and using smaller models for routine ones.
Trim token usage by shortening prompts, truncating context, summarizing history, and setting sensible max_tokens limits on outputs.
Monitor spend continuously with per-user, per-feature, and per-model cost dashboards plus budget alerts to catch runaway usage before it becomes expensive.
